title: Evaluate an Expression

concept.title: Multiplication binds tighter than addition
body: In `3+2*2` the product is calculated first. A neat way to respect this without a stack is to keep two values: `total`, the sum of all finished terms, and `last`, the term that is still being built. A `+` or `-` finishes the last term (add it to `total`) and starts a new term. A `*` or `/` changes only the last term.

Read the digits of a number one by one (`num = num * 10 + digit`) and process the previous number when the next operator (or the end, imitated by an extra `+`) arrives. Division of whole numbers rounds towards zero: in Python do not use `//` on negative values directly.

statement: Evaluate an arithmetic expression that contains positive whole numbers and the operators `+`, `-`, `*` and `/`, without spaces and without parentheses. `*` and `/` come before `+` and `-`, and operators of the same kind are applied from left to right. Division of whole numbers rounds towards zero (`7/2 = 3`, and a negative part such as `-7/2` would give `-3`). The expression never divides by zero.
constraints: The expression has between 1 and 200 characters, it starts and ends with a number, and all numbers are between 1 and 10^6.
All intermediate values fit into 64 bits.
hints: Keep a `total` of finished terms and the `last` term in progress.
On `+` or `-`: add `last` to `total` and start a new term (with a negative sign for `-`).
On `*` or `/`: update `last`. Append a sentinel `+` so that the final number is processed too.

explanation: `total` holds the finished terms and `last` the term being built. `*` and `/` change `last` only, `+` and `-` finish it. A sentinel `+` at the end flushes the last number.
